source.title: Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves
source.authors: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger
readSections: Entire arXiv v3 (31 March 2021, the latest version), 49 pages: §§1–8, Appendices A–B and references, read 2026-09-22 (PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.10276v3, SHA-256 5fc8e86f53ee43e9d18e8239a8db986bff74115ddb947abef4902a72dde338a4). The typeset Annals PDF was not accessible, so the published version was not collated.

summary: Proves that a smooth genus-g curve over a number field of degree ≤ d has at most c(g,d)^{1+ρ} rational points, ρ the Mordell–Weil rank (Theorem 1.1, Mazur's question). It also proves uniform Mordell–Lang for curves of large modular height (Theorem 1.2), torsion-point bounds (Corollary 1.3, Theorem 1.4) and the height inequality ĥ_A ≥ c₁h(π) − c₂ on non-degenerate subvarieties of abelian schemes (Theorems 1.6, B.1). Non-degeneracy is defined by the generic rank of the Betti map, constructed with the Betti form. The inequality combines that form with Siu's bigness criterion and Silverman–Tate; with Gao's non-degeneracy of the Faltings–Zhang images and Rémond's Vojta method it gives the counts. The atlas plans heights, Northcott, Manin–Mumford, Siegel moduli and the Hurwitz bound. It lacks Betti maps, the height inequality, moduli of curves with level structure, relative Jacobians and the counting argument.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (uniform bound for rational points on curves)
items.statement: For integers g ≥ 2 and d ≥ 1 there is c = c(g,d) ≥ 1 such that for every smooth (geometrically irreducible, projective) curve C of genus g over a number field F with [F:ℚ] ≤ d: #C(F) ≤ c^{1+ρ}, where ρ = rk Jac(C)(F).
items.locator: Theorem 1.1 and (1.1), pp.1–2, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Answers Mazur's question. Proof §8: Proposition 8.1 when h(τ(s)) is large; otherwise Northcott leaves finitely many Q̄-isomorphism classes, handled by Rémond's bound for each. The constant grows at most polynomially in d (remark after the proof).

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (uniform Mordell–Lang for curves of large modular height)
items.statement: For g ≥ 2 and an immersion ι : A_{g,1} → ℙ^m_{ℚ̄} of the coarse moduli space, there are c₁ = c₁(g, ι) ≥ 0 and c₂ = c₂(g, ι) ≥ 1 such that for every smooth curve C of genus g over ℚ̄, P₀ ∈ C(ℚ̄) and finite-rank Γ ⊆ Jac(C)(ℚ̄) of rank ρ: if h(ι([Jac(C)])) ≥ c₁ then #((C(ℚ̄) − P₀) ∩ Γ) ≤ c₂^{1+ρ}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p.3, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Proof §8 via Proposition 8.1 and the height comparison h(ι(ρ(t))) ≤ c′h_{A_g,M}(t) + c″.

items.name: Corollary 1.3 (torsion points on curves of large height)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2 with c₁, c₂: if h(ι([Jac(C)])) ≥ c₁ then #((C(ℚ̄) − P₀) ∩ Jac(C)(ℚ̄)_tors) ≤ c₂.
items.locator: Corollary 1.3, p.3, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Theorem 1.2 with Γ = Jac(C)(ℚ̄)_tors of rank 0.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (uniform Manin–Mumford over bounded degree)
items.statement: For g ≥ 2 and d ≥ 1 there is c = c(g,d) ≥ 1 such that for every smooth curve C of genus g defined over a number field F ⊆ ℚ̄ with [F:ℚ] ≤ d and every P₀ ∈ C(ℚ̄): #((C(ℚ̄) − P₀) ∩ Jac(C)(ℚ̄)_tors) ≤ c.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p.3; proof p.36, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021) (small-height step incomplete, sourceIssues E6)
items.note: The small-height case needs a bound uniform in P₀ for each of the finitely many curves; Raynaud's theorem alone gives finiteness for each P₀. The statement itself is true: Kühne's later uniform Manin–Mumford (arXiv:2101.10272) removes d entirely.

items.name: Abelian group of finite rank
items.statement: An abelian group Γ has finite rank if Γ ⊗ ℚ is finite-dimensional over ℚ; its rank is dim_ℚ Γ ⊗ ℚ.
items.locator: §1, p.3, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to RP.5 as a source (the atlas plans finitely generated subgroup intersections only).

items.name: Absolute logarithmic Weil height on ℙ^n(ℚ̄)
items.statement: h : ℙ^n_{ℚ̄}(ℚ̄) → [0,∞), the absolute logarithmic Weil height (Bombieri–Gubler §1.5.1), used on ℙ^m and on products via sums.
items.locator: §1, p.2 and §3.1, p.14, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Mathlib `Projectivization.logHeight` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Projectivization.lean:51) for fields with `Height.AdmissibleAbsValues`; the ℚ̄ extension is RP.0/DT.0 work.

items.name: Coarse moduli space A_{g,1} and the immersion ι
items.statement: A_{g,1} is the coarse moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties, an irreducible quasi-projective variety over ℚ̄; [Jac(C)] ∈ A_{g,1}(ℚ̄) is the point of Jac(C); ι : A_{g,1} → ℙ^m is a chosen immersion.
items.locator: §1, p.2, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: PELModuli M6 plans moduli stacks, fine spaces at rigidifying level and coarse comparisons; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.5 plans coarse spaces.

items.name: Fine moduli space A_{g,ℓ} with symplectic level-ℓ structure and universal abelian variety
items.statement: For ℓ ≥ 3, A_g = A_{g,ℓ} is the fine moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with symplectic level-ℓ structure, an irreducible regular quasi-projective variety (one geometric component, fixing a root of unity ζ_ℓ), with universal abelian scheme π : 𝔄_g → A_g, projective over A_g.
items.locator: §1.2, p.6 and §6.1, p.23, citing MFK Thm 7.9 and Oort–Steenbrink Thm 1.9, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: PELModuli M5 (Siegel moduli for every g) and M6 (fine schemes at rigidifying level with universal abelian scheme).

items.name: Hypothesis (Hyp)
items.statement: (Hyp): the abelian scheme A → S carries a principal polarization and a symplectic level-ℓ structure for some ℓ ≥ 3.
items.locator: §1.2, p.5, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II with the height inequality.

items.name: Fine moduli space M_{g,ℓ} of curves with level structure and its universal curve
items.statement: For g ≥ 2, ℓ ≥ 3, M_g = M_{g,ℓ} is the fine moduli space of smooth genus-g curves whose Jacobian carries level-ℓ structure: an irreducible regular quasi-projective variety of dimension 3g − 3 over ℚ̄ with a smooth projective universal curve C_g → M_g of genus-g fibres.
items.locator: §1.2, p.6 and §6.1, p.23, citing Deligne–Mumford (5.14), Oort–Steenbrink Thm 1.8, ACG XVI 2.11, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Not in Tau Ceti StableReduction (which stops before moduli). Routed to the pending StableReductionPartII (id from PAPER-YUAN-26).

items.name: Relative Jacobian and Picard schemes of the universal curve
items.statement: Jac(C_g) = Pic⁰(C_g/M_g) is an abelian scheme with a natural principal polarization and level-ℓ structure (MFK Prop. 6.9); Pic(C_g/M_g) = ⨆_p Pic^p(C_g/M_g) is a group scheme and there is an M_g-morphism C_g → Pic¹(C_g/M_g) (no section of C_g → M_g is assumed).
items.locator: §6.1, pp.23–24, citing MFK Prop. 6.9, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the pending JacobianChallengePartII (relative Jacobians, Pic^d torsors, degree-one Abel map).

items.name: Torelli morphism M_g → A_g and its finiteness
items.statement: Taking Jacobians gives the Torelli morphism τ : M_g → A_g with Cartesian square (6.1) Jac(C_g) ≅ M_g ×_{A_g} 𝔄_g; τ is finite-to-one on ℂ-points but not injective with level structure (Oort–Steenbrink Lemma 1.11). On coarse spaces Torelli's theorem gives injectivity up to isomorphism, used with Northcott in the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.
items.locator: §1.2, p.6; (6.1), p.24; proofs of Theorems 1.1, 1.4, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the pending StableReductionPartII (which plans compactified Torelli).

items.name: Faltings–Zhang morphism D_M
items.statement: For an abelian variety A and M ≥ 1, D_M : A^{M+1} → A^M, (P₀,…,P_M) ↦ (P₁ − P₀, …, P_M − P₀). In families over S → M_g it is the proper S-morphism D_M : C_S^{[M+1]} → 𝔄_g^{[M]} ×_{A_g} S built from Pic¹ × Pic¹ → Jac by differences.
items.note: The single-abelian-variety morphism is routed to RP.5 as a source; its curve-family version rides on the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Mordell conjecture (Faltings) and Mordell–Weil
items.statement: For a smooth curve C of genus ≥ 2 over a number field F, C(F) is finite (Faltings); Jac(C)(F) is finitely generated (Mordell–Weil).
items.locator: §1, p.1, citing [Fal83], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: RP.4 plans Faltings' theorem for curves; RP.1 plans weak Mordell–Weil and finite generation.

items.name: Manin–Mumford (Raynaud)
items.statement: A curve C of genus ≥ 2 embedded in its Jacobian contains only finitely many torsion points.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.4, p.36, citing Raynaud [Ray83], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: RP.5 plans the Manin–Mumford theorem.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 / B.2 (existence of the Betti map)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme π : A → S over a regular irreducible quasi-projective complex S and s₀ ∈ S(ℂ), there are an open neighbourhood Δ of s₀ in S^an and a map b_Δ : A_Δ := π^{-1}(Δ) → T^{2g} with (i) b_Δ|_{A_s(ℂ)} a group isomorphism for each s ∈ Δ, (ii) every fibre b_Δ^{-1}(ξ) complex analytic, (iii) (b_Δ, π) : A_Δ → T^{2g} × Δ a real-analytic isomorphism. For connected Δ, b_Δ is unique up to GL_{2g}(ℤ).
items.locator: Proposition 2.1, p.8 (under (Hyp)); Proposition B.2, p.41 (general); proofs §2.1, §2.3, B.1, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Constructed on A_{g,D,ℓ} from ℂ^g × ℍ_g → ℝ^{2g} (inverse of (a,b,Z) ↦ (Da + Zb, Z)), pulled back along the classifying map, and descended from a finite étale level cover. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Real-coordinate uniformization of the universal abelian variety
items.statement: X_{2g,a} := ℝ^{2g} × ℍ_g with complex structure (a,b,Z) ↦ (a + Zb, Z) is the universal covering of 𝔄_g^an; P_{2g,a} = V_{2g} ⋊ Sp_{2g} acts by (v,h)·(v′,Z) = (v + hv′, hZ), and 𝔄_g^an is the quotient by a congruence subgroup of P_{2g,a}(ℚ).
items.note: Mixed Shimura datum of the universal abelian variety. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3 (the Betti form upstairs)
items.statement: ω̂_univ := √−1 ∂∂̄(2 (Im w)ᵀ (Im Z)^{−1} (Im w)) on ℂ^g × ℍ_g is a closed semi-positive (1,1)-form equal to √−1 (dZ Y^{−1} Im w − dw)ᵀ ∧ Y^{−1} (dZ̄ Y^{−1} Im w − dw̄) with Y = Im Z, and Ñ*ω̂_univ = N²ω̂_univ for Ñ(w,Z) = (Nw, Z).
items.locator: Lemma 2.3 and (2.1), pp.8–10, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.4 and Corollary 2.5 (Betti form in real coordinates)
items.statement: Under (a,b,Z) ↦ (a + Zb, Z), ω̂_univ = 2 (da)ᵀ ∧ db. Consequently ω̂_univ vanishes on the smooth locus of an irreducible 1-dimensional analytic set Ĉ iff Ĉ ⊆ {r} × ℍ_g for some r ∈ ℝ^{2g}.
items.locator: Lemma 2.4 and Corollary 2.5, pp.10–11, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 (descent of the Betti form)
items.statement: ω̂_univ is invariant under P_{2g,a}(ℝ) and descends to a semi-positive (1,1)-form ω_univ on 𝔄_g^an with [N]*ω_univ = N²ω_univ.
items.locator: Lemma 2.6, p.11, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Proposition 2.2(i)–(ii) (the Betti form)
items.statement: Under (Hyp) there is a closed (1,1)-form ω on A^an, ω := ι*ω_univ for the classifying map ι : A → 𝔄_g, which is semi-positive and satisfies [N]*ω = N²ω for all N ∈ ℤ.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2 (i)–(ii), p.8; §2.3, pp.12–13, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Proposition 2.2(iii) and Proposition 2.7 (Betti form versus Betti rank)
items.statement: For an irreducible X ⊆ A of dimension d and open Δ ⊆ S^an with X^{sm,an} ∩ A_Δ ≠ ∅: (ω|_{X^{sm,an}})^{∧d} ≢ 0 iff max_{x} rank_ℝ (db_Δ|_{X^{sm,an}})_x = 2d.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2(iii), p.8; Proposition 2.7, pp.11–12; general case (2.5)–(2.7), pp.12–13, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Definition 1.5 / B.4 (non-degenerate subvariety)
items.statement: An irreducible subvariety X of an abelian scheme A → S is non-degenerate if there is a non-empty open Δ ⊆ S^{sm,an} with Betti map b_Δ such that X^{sm,an} ∩ A_Δ ≠ ∅ and max_{x ∈ X^{sm}(ℂ) ∩ A_Δ} rank_ℝ (db_Δ|_{X^{sm,an}})_x = 2 dim X; for X over ℚ̄, after base change to ℂ.
items.locator: Definition 1.5, p.5; Definition B.4, p.43, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma B.3 (generic Betti rank is birational)
items.statement: For a Betti map b_Δ, an irreducible X with X^an ∩ A_Δ ≠ ∅ and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X, the maximal ranks of db_Δ on X^{sm} ∩ A_Δ and on U^{sm} ∩ A_Δ agree.
items.locator: Lemma B.3, pp.42–43, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Theorem 6.2 (non-degeneracy of D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}), Gao)
items.statement: Let S be irreducible with a quasi-finite morphism S → M_g, g ≥ 2, M ≥ 3g − 2. Then D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}) ⊆ 𝔄_g^{[M]} ×_{A_g} S is non-degenerate.
items.locator: Theorem 6.2 and proof, pp.26–28, citing Gao [Gao20a, Thm. 1.2′, Thm. 1.3(ii)], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Proof: with a section, Gao's Theorem 1.3(ii) applies to the Abel–Jacobi image (hypotheses (a)–(c): relative dimension 1, curves generate, finite stabilizer for g ≥ 2) with M ≥ dim S + 1 ≤ 3g − 2; in general pass to a quasi-finite étale cover with a section and transport the Betti map. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Remark 3.1 (projective presentation of an abelian scheme)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme π : A → S over S ⊆ S̄ ⊆ ℙ^m and a symmetric ample L₀ on the generic fibre, there is an S-ample L on A restricting to L₀^{⊗l} (l ≥ 4) with [−1]*L ≅ L trivial along the zero section (Raynaud, Faisceaux amples XI 1.13, 1.3a); a power is S-very ample and L ⊗ π*M gives a closed immersion A → ℙ^n × S whose generic fibre is projectively normal.
items.locator: Remark 3.1, p.13; §6.1, p.24 (Raynaud XI 1.4), arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 as a source.

items.name: Naive and fibrewise Néron–Tate heights on an abelian scheme
items.statement: For P = (P′, π(P)) ∈ A(ℚ̄) ⊆ ℙ^n × ℙ^m, h(P) = h(P′) + h(π(P)); ĥ_A(P) = lim_N h([N]P)/N² is the fibrewise Néron–Tate height, a quadratic form on each A_s(ℚ̄); normalized ĥ_{A,L₀} = ĥ_A/l.
items.note: RP.0 plans the height machine and Néron–Tate heights.

items.name: Remark 3.2 (normalization independent of the model)
items.statement: If L′ on A also restricts to L₀^{⊗l} on the generic fibre, then L′ ⊗ L^{−1} is a pullback from S (EGA IV 21.4.13), so L|_{A_s} and L′|_{A_s} induce the same Néron–Tate height for all s; ĥ_{A,L₀} depends only on L₀.
items.locator: Remark 3.2, p.14, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Line bundles trivial on the generic fibre come from the base
items.statement: For an abelian (more generally, proper flat with geometrically integral fibres) scheme A → S over a normal base, a line bundle on A trivial on the generic fibre is isomorphic to π*K for a line bundle K on S (EGA IV 21.4.13).
items.locator: §3.1, p.14; Remark 3.2, p.14; proof of Proposition A.2, p.38, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Compactly supported cut-off θω of the Betti form
items.statement: For s₀ ∈ S^an, a relatively compact contractible neighbourhood Δ and a smooth bump ϑ : S^an → [0,1] with compact support K ⊆ Δ and ϑ(s₀) = 1, θ := ϑ ∘ π; θω is a semi-positive smooth (1,1)-form with compact support in π^{-1}(K), not necessarily closed. For non-degenerate X take s₀ = π(P₀) with (ω|_X)^{∧d}_{P₀} > 0.
items.locator: §3.2 and Remark 3.3, pp.14–15, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II with the height inequality.

items.name: Graph construction X_N and the line bundles F, M
items.statement: Γ_N = {(P, [N]P)} ⊆ A ×_S A; X_N the graph of [N]|_X and X̄_N its Zariski closure in ℙ^n × ℙ^n × ℙ^m, dim X̄_N = dim X; F = O(0,1,1)|_{X̄_N}, M = O(0,0,1)|_{X̄_N}; h_{X̄_N,F}(P_N) = h([N]P) and h_{X̄_N,M}(P_N) = h(π(P)) up to O(1).
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Siu's bigness criterion
items.statement: For nef line bundles F, M on an irreducible projective variety of dimension d, F ⊗ M^{−1} is big if (F^d) > d (F^{d−1}·M).
items.locator: §4, pp.16, 22, citing Lazarsfeld [Laz04, Thm. 2.2.15], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Positivity of intersections on multiprojective space (Fulton 12.2(a))
items.statement: On a variety whose tangent bundle is globally generated (e.g. a product of projective spaces), the intersection class of equidimensional V₁,…,V_r is represented by a non-negative cycle whose support contains every proper component; hence every effective Weil divisor on multiprojective space is nef.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3, p.20, citing Fulton [Ful98, Cor. 12.2(a), Ex. 12.2.1], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Integration of positive forms over analytic subsets and intersection numbers
items.statement: Smooth compactly supported forms integrate over complex analytic subsets (Lelong); wedge products of semi-positive (1,1)-forms are positive (Demailly III.1.11, III.2.7); on a compact projective variety, ∫_{X^an} α^{∧d} for a Fubini–Study representative α of O(1,…,1) equals the intersection number (O(1,…,1)^{·d}·[X]) (Voisin Thm. 11.21).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.2, pp.17–18, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to ComplexComparisonPartII C5 as a source.

items.name: Multiplication by 2 by quartic polynomials
items.statement: On a projectively normal abelian variety embedded by a symmetric very ample L, [2] is given by homogeneous polynomials f₀,…,f_n of degree 4 with no common zeros on A (Serre, in Waldschmidt App. II, Cor. 2); spreading out gives bihomogeneous polynomials of bidegree (4, D′) valid off a proper closed π^{-1}(π(Z)), and iterates for [2^l] of bidegree (4^l, (4^l − 1)D′/3).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3, pp.19–20, (4.11), citing [Wal87], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.2 (lower bound for the top self-intersection)
items.statement: If X^an has a smooth point where (ω|_{X^{sm,an}})^{∧d} > 0, there is κ > 0 independent of N with (F^{·d}) ≥ κ N^{2d} on X̄_N for all N ∈ ℕ.
items.locator: Proposition 4.2 and proof, pp.17–19, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: C α − ω ≥ 0 on A_Δ, pull back by [N] using [N]*ω = N²ω, compare ∫(C[N]*(θα))^d ≥ N^{2d}∫(θω)^d, then integrate over X̄_N. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 4.3 (upper bound for the mixed intersection)
items.statement: For d ≥ 1 there is c > 0 depending on the data such that for every N a power of 2: (M·F^{·(d−1)}) ≤ c N^{2(d−1)} on X̄_N.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3 and proof, pp.19–21, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Cut out X̄_N by the iterated quartic polynomials and apply Fulton positivity. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (height inequality on the total space)
items.statement: If X^an has a smooth point where (ω|_X)^{∧d} > 0, there is c₁ > 0 such that for every N a power of 2 there are a Zariski open dense U_N ⊆ X over ℚ̄ and c₂(N) with h([N]P) ≥ c₁ N² h(π(P)) − c₂(N) for all P ∈ U_N(ℚ̄).
items.locator: Proposition 4.1, p.16; proof §4.3, pp.21–22, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Siu applied to F^{⊗q} ⊗ M^{⊗−qc₁N²} with 0 < c₁cd < κ. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Theorem A.1 (Silverman–Tate, Cartier-divisor version)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme π : A → S over a regular irreducible quasi-projective S/ℚ̄ with a closed immersion A → ℙ^n × S, S ⊆ S̄ ⊆ ℙ^m, L = O(1,1)|_A symmetric on the generic fibre: there is c > 0 with |ĥ_A(P) − h(P)| ≤ c·max{1, h_S(π(P))} for all P ∈ A(ℚ̄).
items.locator: Theorem A.1 and proof, pp.36–40, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021); Silverman [Sil83, Thm. A]
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Proposition A.2 (duplication estimate)
items.statement: There is c₁ > 0 with |h([2]P) − 4h(P)| ≤ c₁ max{1, h_S(π(P))} for all P ∈ A(ℚ̄).
items.locator: Proposition A.2 and proof, pp.37–40, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Graph closure A′ of [2]; F′ = [2]*L ⊗ ρ*L^{⊗−4} trivial on the generic fibre, hence a pullback; resolve S̄ and A (Hironaka) and bound a Cartier divisor supported over the boundary by pullbacks of effective divisors E_i avoiding any given π(P); finitely many choices cover S. Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Resolution of singularities in characteristic 0 (Hironaka)
items.statement: A variety over a field of characteristic 0 admits a proper birational morphism from a regular variety that is an isomorphism over the regular locus; in particular the compactifications S̄ and Ā can be desingularized without changing S and A.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.2, pp.38–39, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7 plans characteristic-zero resolution preserving the regular locus.

items.name: Cartier and Weil divisors on regular and normal schemes
items.statement: On a normal integral scheme an effective Weil divisor that is Cartier is an effective Cartier divisor with the same support; on a regular scheme Cartier = Weil; line bundles extend from an open subset of a regular scheme; pullbacks of Cartier divisors along dominant morphisms and inverse images of effective Cartier divisors (Görtz–Wedhorn 11.38–11.49).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.2, pp.38–39, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (height inequality under (Hyp))
items.statement: Let S be regular irreducible quasi-projective over ℚ̄, Zariski open in S̄ ⊆ ℙ^m, π : A → S an abelian scheme with (Hyp), presented by A → ℙ^n × S coming on the generic fibre from L^{⊗l}, l ≥ 4, L symmetric ample. If X ⊆ A is closed irreducible over ℚ̄, dominates S and is non-degenerate, there are c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X with ĥ_A(P) ≥ c₁ h(π(P)) − c₂ for all P ∈ U(ℚ̄).
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p.5; proof §5, pp.22–23, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Proposition 4.1 with Silverman–Tate; fix N a power of 2 with N² ≥ 2c₀/c₁ to kill the Zimmer constant. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Theorem B.1 (height inequality, general form)
items.statement: Let π : A → S be an abelian scheme over an irreducible quasi-projective S/ℚ̄ with symmetric relatively ample L and an ample M on a compactification S̄. If X ⊆ A is an irreducible (not necessarily closed) non-degenerate subvariety over ℚ̄, there are c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X with ĥ_{A,L}(P) ≥ c₁ h_{S̄,M}(π(P)) − c₂ for all P ∈ U(ℚ̄).
items.locator: Theorem B.1 and proof, pp.40–47, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021) (dévissage labels misprinted, sourceIssues E5)
items.note: Seven dévissages: closure, dominance, regular base, isogenous to principal (Mumford §23 Cor. 1 over the function field), principal polarization, level-ℓ structure after finite étale base change, then Theorem 1.6 with ĥ_{A,L} = ĥ_A/4. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Isogeny to a principal polarization in families
items.statement: Every abelian variety over an algebraically closed field is isogenous to a principally polarized one (Mumford §23 Cor. 1); applied to the geometric generic fibre, after a quasi-finite étale dominant S′ → S and shrinking there is a principally polarized A′₀ → S′ with an S′-isogeny A′₀ → A ×_S S′ (Raynaud, Faisceaux amples XI 1.4, Lemme XI 1.15). An abelian scheme over a regular base carries a polarization of some type D (Genestier–Ngô §2.1).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem B.1 (fourth and fifth dévissages), pp.44–45; proof of Proposition B.2, p.41, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 as a source.

items.name: Moduli A_{g,D,ℓ} of type-D polarized abelian varieties with level structure
items.statement: For a polarization type D = diag(d₁,…,d_g) and ℓ ≥ 3 prime to d_g, A_{g,D,ℓ} is a fine moduli space (Genestier–Ngô Thm. 2.3.1) with universal abelian variety, uniformized by ℍ_g with period lattice Dℤ^g + Zℤ^g.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition B.2, p.41, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: PELModuli M5 includes at least one non-principal polarization type and M6 the fine spaces at rigidifying level.

items.name: Lemma 6.1 (uniform degree and height of the Abel–Jacobi curves)
items.statement: There is c such that for all s ∈ M_g(ℚ̄): (i) deg(C_s − P) ≤ c for all P ∈ 𝔄_{g,τ(s)}(ℚ̄); (ii) some P_s ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) has h(C_s − P_s) ≤ c·max{1, h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))}.
items.locator: Lemma 6.1 and proof, pp.25–26, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Quasi-section of C_g → M_g (EGA IV 17.16.3(ii)), constructible images, Bézout for (i) and Philippon's arithmetic Bézout [Phi95, Thm. 3] for (ii). Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Heights of projective subvarieties and arithmetic Bézout
items.statement: For an irreducible X ⊆ ℙ^n over ℚ̄, deg X and the Bost–Gillet–Soulé height h(X); Philippon's arithmetic Bézout theorem bounds h and deg of the components of an intersection in terms of those of the intersecting varieties.
items.locator: §6.1, p.25; proof of Lemma 6.1, p.26, citing [BGS94], [Phi95, Thm. 3], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Bézout's theorem (Fulton Ex. 8.4.6)
items.statement: The sum of the degrees of the irreducible components of an intersection of subvarieties of projective space is at most the product of their degrees.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 6.1 and 6.3, pp.26, 28, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Quasi-sections of smooth surjective morphisms
items.statement: A smooth surjective morphism admits, étale-locally on the target, a section: there are an affine S and a surjective quasi-finite étale S → M_g through which S → C_g factors (EGA IV 17.16.3(ii)).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.1, p.26, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (many points escape a proper subvariety of C^M)
items.statement: For an irreducible curve C ⊆ ℙ^n_k and a Zariski closed Z ⊆ (ℙ^n_k)^M with C^M ⊄ Z, there is B depending only on M, deg C and deg Z such that every Σ ⊆ C(k) with #Σ ≥ B satisfies Σ^M ⊄ Z(k).
items.locator: Lemma 6.3 and proof, p.28, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Induction on M splitting Z ∩ C^M by whether the first projection is dominant. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Hurwitz bound for automorphisms
items.statement: A smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 has at most 84(g − 1) automorphisms.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.4, p.29, citing [Hur92], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves layer 11 plans automorphisms and the Hurwitz bound.

items.name: Lemma 6.4 (few base points force a proper subvariety)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over ℚ̄, a smooth curve C ⊆ A of genus g ≥ 2 and an irreducible proper closed Z ⊊ D_M(C^{M+1}): #{P ∈ C(ℚ̄) : (C − P)^M ⊆ Z} ≤ 84(g − 1).
items.locator: Lemma 6.4 and proof, pp.28–29, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Two such P₀, P₁ give (C − P₀)^M = Z = (C − P₁)^M, so P₁ − P₀ stabilizes C; stabilizer elements act as automorphisms. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (Néron–Tate distance between points on curves)
items.statement: For an irreducible closed S ⊆ M_g over ℚ̄ there are c₁, c₂, c₃, c₄ > 0 such that for s ∈ S(ℚ̄) with h_{A_g,M}(τ(s)) ≥ c₁ there is Ξ_s ⊆ C_s(ℚ̄), #Ξ_s ≤ c₂, with every P ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) satisfying (i) P ∈ Ξ_s, or (ii) #{Q ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) : ĥ(Q − P) ≤ h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))/c₃} < c₄.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1 and proof, pp.29–31, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Induction on dim S: Theorem 6.2 plus Theorem 1.6 on D_M(C^{[M+1]}_{S^{sm}}) with M = 3g − 2; Lemma 6.4 bounds the exceptional base points; Lemma 6.3 gives c₄; c₃ = 2M/c. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Comparison of heights under morphisms (Silverman Lemma 4)
items.statement: For a morphism of quasi-projective varieties and ample line bundles on compactifications, there are c′ > 0, c″ ≥ 0 with h_{M′}(x) ≥ c′h_M(f(x)) − c″ (e.g. h(s) ≥ c″h_{A_g,M}(τ(s)) − c‴ on M̄_g, and h(ι(ρ(t))) ≤ c′h_{A_g,M}(t) + c″).
items.locator: (7.1), p.29; proofs of Theorems 1.1, 1.2, pp.35–36; Theorem B.1 p.45, citing [Sil11, Lemma 4], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: RP.0 plans the height machine with pullback laws.

items.name: Northcott property
items.statement: There are only finitely many points of ℙ^n(ℚ̄) of bounded degree and bounded height.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4, pp.34–36, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: RP.0 plans Northcott from the audited height supplier; Mathlib has `Northcott (mulHeight₁ (K := K))` for number fields but not points of bounded degree over ℚ̄.

items.name: Lemma 8.2 (Rémond: large points via Vojta and Mumford)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A ⊆ ℙ^n embedded by a basis of H⁰(A, L), L symmetric very ample and A projectively normal, and an irreducible curve C ⊆ A not a translate of an algebraic subgroup, there is c = c(n, deg C) ≥ 1 with #{P ∈ C(ℚ̄) ∩ Γ : ĥ_L(P) > c·max{1, h(C), c_NT, h₁}} ≤ c^ρ for every finite-rank Γ ⊆ A(ℚ̄) of rank ρ.
items.locator: Lemma 8.2, p.32, citing [DGH19, Cor. 2.3] and Rémond [Rém00a, Rém00b], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: The constants c_NT and h₁ of an embedded abelian variety
items.statement: c_NT ≥ 0 with |ĥ_L − h| ≤ c_NT on A(ℚ̄); h₁ is the Weil height of the coefficient vector of bihomogeneous polynomials P_ij of bidegree (2,2) with f*(p₁*ξ_i ⊗ p₂*ξ_j) = P_ij(p₁*ξ, p₂*ξ) for f(P,Q) = (P+Q, P−Q) (existence: Rémond [Rém00b, Prop. 5.2]).
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Bounds (8.4) and (8.7) for c_NT and h₁ over A_g
items.statement: For A = 𝔄_{g,τ(s)} with the embedding of §6.1: c_NT ≤ c·max{1, h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))} (Silverman–Tate) and one can choose the P_ij with h₁ ≤ c·max{1, h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))}, obtained by Cramer's rule from the linear system (8.6) at finitely many torsion points, which are Zariski dense.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 8.1, pp.32–33, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Ball-packing lemma (Rémond Lemme 6.1)
items.statement: In a Euclidean space of dimension ρ, any subset of a closed ball of radius R is covered by at most (1 + 2R/r)^ρ closed balls of radius r ≤ R centred at points of the subset.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 8.1, p.34, citing [Rém00a, Lemme 6.1], arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 8.1 (count for curves of large modular height)
items.statement: There are c₁ ≥ 0, c₂ ≥ 1 such that for s ∈ M_g(ℚ̄) with h_{A_g,M}(τ(s)) ≥ c₁, every finite-rank Γ ⊆ 𝔄_{g,τ(s)}(ℚ̄) of rank ρ and every P₀ ∈ C_s(ℚ̄): #((C_s(ℚ̄) − P₀) ∩ Γ) ≤ c₂^{1+ρ}.
items.locator: Proposition 8.1 and proof, pp.31–34, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Large points by Lemma 8.2 with (8.4), (8.7), (8.8); small points by ball packing with radius r² = max{1,h}/c₃ and Proposition 7.1(ii); general base point via Γ′ = ⟨Γ, P₀ − P_s⟩. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Finitely many moduli points of small height and bounded degree
items.statement: If h_{A_g,M}(τ(s)) < c₁ and C is defined over F with [F:ℚ] ≤ d, then τ(s), s and F′ = F(s) lie in finite sets depending on g, d, ℓ (Northcott, finiteness of τ); the remaining curves are twists in finitely many F′-isomorphism classes, and Rémond's bound for a single curve (David–Philippon [DP02, p.643]) finishes Theorem 1.1.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, pp.34–35, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Polynomial growth of c(g,d) in d
items.statement: The constant c(g,d) of Theorem 1.1 can be chosen to grow at most polynomially in d: in the small-height case the stable Faltings height of 𝔄_{g,τ(s)} is bounded (Faltings [Fal83, §3], Faltings–Chai V.4.4–4.5) and so is the David–Philippon height (Bost–David, [DP02, Cor. 6.9], Pazuki), and Rémond's bound depends polynomially on D·max{1, h_DP} with D ≤ [F′:F]d.
items.locator: Remark after the proof of Theorem 1.1, p.35, arXiv v3 (31 March 2021)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

routes.reason: RP.0 owns the height machine and Néron–Tate heights, RP.5 subvarieties of abelian varieties. The paper is a source there for the Silverman–Tate comparison in families with its duplication estimate, the model-independence of the fibrewise Néron–Tate height, Serre's quartic representation of [2], finite-rank groups and the Faltings–Zhang morphism. These are classical height and abelian-variety tools; the families-specific inequalities go in the Part II.

A2 owns polarizations and relatively ample symmetric line bundles on abelian schemes. The paper uses Raynaud's existence of S-ample symmetric bundles and projective presentations (Faisceaux amples XI 1.4, 1.13), Mumford's isogeny to a principal polarization, its extension over an étale cover (XI 1.15) and polarization types over a regular base. These are exactly A2 material, so the paper is a source for it.

SF.0 owns general scheme theory and SF.5 intersection theory. The proofs need EGA IV 21.4.13 (line bundles trivial on the generic fibre), Cartier/Weil divisor facts on regular and normal schemes (Görtz–Wedhorn 11.38–11.49), étale quasi-sections (EGA IV 17.16.3), Siu's bigness criterion, Fulton's positivity on multiprojective space and Bézout. They are general tools, so the paper is a source for those layers.

C5 builds the integration map from algebraic de Rham forms to the analytic side. Proposition 4.2 needs integration of compactly supported smooth forms over analytic subsets (Lelong), positivity of wedge products of semi-positive (1,1)-forms, and the equality ∫α^d = intersection number for a Fubini–Study representative. That is the integration comparison this layer owns.

routes.title: Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli, Part II: Betti maps and non-degenerate subvarieties
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 under the same id; this paper is its foundational source. Build on complex uniformization of polarized abelian schemes in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 and its Siegel universal family, fine moduli A_{g,D,ℓ} from PELModuli M5–M6, analytic comparison from ComplexComparisonPartII C0 and C4, Tau Ceti HodgeStructures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures) for weight-one variations, and mixed Ax–Schanuel from LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6 and its proposed Part II. State and prove, as in Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger (Ann. Math. 194 (2021)): Proposition 2.1/B.2, existence and GL_{2g}(ℤ)-uniqueness of the Betti map b_Δ : A_Δ → T^{2g} for any abelian scheme over a regular quasi-projective complex base (fibrewise group isomorphism, analytic fibres, real-analytic trivialization), via the mixed-Shimura uniformization ℝ^{2g} × ℍ_g of 𝔄_g and descent from a finite étale level cover; Lemmas 2.3–2.6, the Betti form ω̂_univ = √−1∂∂̄(2(Im w)ᵀ(Im Z)^{−1}(Im w)) = 2(da)ᵀ∧db, semi-positive and invariant under V_{2g} ⋊ Sp_{2g}(ℝ), descending to ω with [N]*ω = N²ω; Proposition 2.2(iii)/2.7, (ω|_X)^{∧d} ≢ 0 iff the Betti rank on X is 2d; Definition 1.5/B.4 non-degeneracy and Lemma B.3; Theorem 6.2 (Gao, Compos. Math. 156 (2020), Thm. 1.2′/1.3): D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}) is non-degenerate for S → M_g quasi-finite and M ≥ 3g − 2. Include Gao's general criterion and degeneracy loci as in the GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 brief. Acceptance: ω vanishes on the smooth locus of a curve exactly when the curve lies in a fibre of b_Δ (Corollary 2.5); a torsion section is degenerate; every subvariety of a constant family is non-degenerate.
routes.reason: The Betti map and Betti form are not in the atlas. This paper constructs them in general, and GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 already proposed this Part II id, so the two coalesce.

routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang
routes.brief: Same id as the pending PAPER-YUAN-26 and PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 routes. This paper supplies the height inequality those routes import and the curve case of uniform Mordell–Lang. Import the height machine, Néron–Tate heights, Silverman–Tate and Northcott from HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0, Mordell–Weil, Faltings and Manin–Mumford from RP.1, RP.4 and RP.5, Siegel moduli from PELModuli M5–M6, compactifications from ShimuraCompactifications C5, Betti maps and non-degeneracy from AbelianSchemesBettiMapsPartII, moduli of curves with level structure and Torelli from StableReductionPartII, relative Jacobians from JacobianChallengePartII, intersection theory, Siu and Fulton positivity from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5, and the integration comparison from ComplexComparisonPartII C5. State and prove (Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger, Ann. Math. 194 (2021)): Theorem 1.6 and its general form Theorem B.1, ĥ_{A,L}(P) ≥ c₁h_{S̄,M}(π(P)) − c₂ on a Zariski open dense subset of any non-degenerate X, via the graph construction, Propositions 4.1–4.3 (κN^{2d} ≤ (F^d), (M·F^{d−1}) ≤ cN^{2(d−1)}) and Siu's criterion, with the seven dévissage steps; Lemma 6.1 (uniform degree, and height ≪ max{1, h(τ(s))}, of Abel–Jacobi curves via arithmetic Bézout); Lemmas 6.3 and 6.4; Proposition 7.1 (Néron–Tate distance alternative); Lemma 8.2 (Rémond), the bounds (8.4) and (8.7) for c_NT and h₁; Proposition 8.1; Theorem 1.1 (#C(F) ≤ c(g,d)^{1+ρ}, with polynomial dependence on d), Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3 and Theorem 1.4. For Theorem 1.4 supply the bound uniform in the base point for the finitely many small-height curves (sourceIssues E6). Acceptance: the constants do not depend on the height of C; for rank 0 and torsion the count is independent of the height once h(τ(s)) ≥ c₁.
routes.reason: The uniformity programme is the Part II already proposed under this id by YUAN-26 and GAO-GE-KUHNE-26. DGH provides its height inequality and the curve case, so it coalesces rather than proposing a new roadmap.

routes.title: Stable reduction of curves and stable maps, Part II: moduli of curves and stable compactifications
routes.brief: This is the pending PAPER-YUAN-26 Part II of the same id, and its brief remains binding. This paper adds two consumer requirements. First, the fine moduli space M_{g,ℓ} of smooth genus-g curves (g ≥ 2) with symplectic level-ℓ structure (ℓ ≥ 3), a single geometrically irreducible component over ℚ̄ fixed by choosing ζ_ℓ, regular, quasi-projective of dimension 3g − 3, with a smooth projective universal curve C_g → M_g (Deligne–Mumford (5.14), Oort–Steenbrink Thm. 1.8). Second, the Torelli morphism τ : M_g → A_{g,ℓ}, with the Cartesian square Jac(C_g) ≅ M_g ×_{A_g} 𝔄_g, finite-to-one on ℂ-points (Oort–Steenbrink Lemma 1.11) and injective up to isomorphism on coarse spaces (Torelli's theorem). Export both to HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII. Import fine moduli of abelian varieties from PELModuli M5–M6, and relative Jacobians from JacobianChallengePartII. Acceptance: τ is not injective at level ℓ ≥ 3 (the hyperelliptic involution acts on level structures), and a quasi-finite S → M_g pulls back a universal curve with irreducible fibred powers.
routes.reason: Tau Ceti StableReduction stops before moduli spaces of curves. YUAN-26 already proposed this Part II, and DGH needs the fine level-ℓ moduli and the Torelli morphism, which fit inside it.

routes.title: The Jacobian challenge, Part II: relative Jacobians and theta identities
routes.brief: This is the pending PAPER-YUAN-26 Part II of the same id, and its brief remains binding. This paper requires the relative Picard group scheme Pic(C_g/M_g) = ⨆_p Pic^p(C_g/M_g) of the universal curve, the relative Jacobian Jac(C_g) = Pic⁰ as an abelian scheme with its natural principal polarization and level-ℓ structure (MFK Prop. 6.9), and the M_g-morphism C_g → Pic¹(C_g/M_g) without a section of C_g → M_g. It also requires the difference map Pic¹ ×_{M_g} Pic¹ → Jac, from which the Faltings–Zhang morphism C_S^{[M+1]} → Jac^{[M]} is built for any S → M_g. Import abelian schemes and duality from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1–A3 and representability from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2–R09.3. Acceptance: over a point, the construction recovers the Abel–Jacobi embedding C − P₀ → Jac(C) once P₀ is chosen.
routes.reason: Tau Ceti's Jacobian challenge works over a field. YUAN-26 already proposed this Part II for relative Jacobians, and DGH needs the relative Picard and Jacobian of the universal curve, so it joins that route.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.4, p.36 (arXiv v3; published Annals version not collated)
sourceIssues.printed: "By the Northcott property and Torelli's Theorem, there are up-to Q̄-isomophism only finitely many C_Q̄'s … such that h(ι([Jac(C_Q̄)])) < c1. By applying Raynaud's result on the Manin–Mumford Conjecture to each one of these finitely many curves separately, we obtain Theorem 1.4."
sourceIssues.correction: For each of the finitely many curves C a bound for #((C − P₀) ∩ Jac(C)_tors) uniform in P₀ ∈ C(ℚ̄) is needed, because Theorem 1.4 quantifies over all P₀. For g ≥ 3 it follows from Raynaud's theorem for the surface C − C ⊆ Jac(C): its torsion lies in finitely many points and elliptic torsion cosets, and a coset t + E pulls back to a curve in C × C with no component C × {P₀}, so each P₀ meets it in boundedly many points. For g = 2, C − C = Jac(C), and a uniform Manin–Mumford for the translates C − P₀ is required, e.g. Kühne's later uniform Manin–Mumford theorem (arXiv:2101.10272), which proves Theorem 1.4 without the dependence on d.
sourceIssues.reason: Raynaud's theorem gives, for each embedding C − P₀ ⊆ Jac(C), a finite set, with no control of its size as P₀ varies over the infinitely many points of C(ℚ̄). The statement is true, but the displayed step does not prove it.
